land.text: all of Egypt as the vassal kingdom of Psamtik I held it at independence (the Delta from 664, Upper Egypt from 656), drawn with the -615 shape

predecessors.note: assyrian-egypt (Psamtik I's vassal kingdom: found -664 with Lower Egypt, gains Upper Egypt from kingdom-of-kush in -656) dissolves into this state at independence, about 655 ('Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE', Assyrian conquest of Egypt page). This dossier starts at independence rather than at the dynasty page's 'Established: 664 BC', so that the Delta is not drawn twice in 664-655; Upper Egypt passes from kingdom-of-kush to assyrian-egypt in -656, not to this state.

land.text: Egypt, conquered by Cambyses II in 525 ('First Achaemenid conquest of Egypt', 'First Egyptian Satrapy'); Cyprus had already passed to Persia in 545 (Ancient history of Cyprus page)

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Twenty-seventh Dynasty of Egypt' (the Persian kings as pharaohs). Cliopatria's Achaemenid shape of -530..-501 holds only Sinai of Egypt (gazetteer check), so the achaemenid-empire dossier must add the Nile land from 525; until it does, Cliopatria covers 525-501 only by keeping this row to -501.

capitals.name: Sais (Sa el-Hagar)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Sais'; 'also called the Saite Period after the city of Sais'. Coordinates from the gazetteer's Sais. Sais was already Psamtik I's seat as vassal king from 664 (see assyrian-egypt).

rulers.name: Psamtik I
rulers.note: Manetho: 54 years. King from 664 as an Assyrian vassal (see assyrian-egypt); independent from about 655, where this dossier begins.

rulers.name: Apries
rulers.note: Deposed by Amasis II in 570; later 'returned to Egypt at the head of a Babylonian army, defeated, and likely killed'.

rulers.name: Psamtik III
rulers.note: About six months, per Herodotus; captured and later executed by Cambyses II.

correction.text: New keyframe: all of Egypt, from the Delta to Thebes, drawn with the shape Cliopatria gives from -615 (the page: Psamtik I's navy 'peacefully took control of Thebes and effectively unified all of Egypt' in 656)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's row begins in -615, 40 years after independence; its Assyrian Egypt row (-650..-616) covers these years instead. 'Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE' and 'was able to declare outright independence from Assyria'; Thebes fell to him in 656 (Assyrian conquest of Egypt page). The 664-655 vassal years belong to assyrian-egypt, so the -664 Delta keyframe of the first version is dropped. Infobox gives no area.

452,849 km2 (about 381,000 km2 on the grid). Amasis II page: 'His kingdom consisted probably of Egypt only, as far as the First Cataract' (the shape's south edge, 23.5N, lies a little south of Aswan); neither page gives an area. The Cyprus page dates the Egyptian conquest of Cyprus to 570 ('In 570 BC, Cyprus was conquered by Egypt under Amasis II'), 20 years before Cliopatria's -550 shape, so -570..-551 take the next shape. The Western Desert west of 28.3E is outside the shape; the pages opened do not mention it. The 612 BC attempts to regain the Near East were 'driven back' and the Levant 609-605 is a contest, not a holding (see ledger).

correction.text: Shape unchanged, years only: Egypt east of 28.3E, Sinai included, holds -615..-571; Cliopatria keeps it to -551, but Cyprus joins Egypt in 570

keyframe_review.note: 464,287 km2: the -615 shape plus Cyprus. Amasis II page: 'to this he added Cyprus', 'the first pharaoh to conquer Cyprus after Thutmose III', no year; the Cyprus page gives 570 and the end in 545. Cliopatria's -550 is 20 years late and its Cyprus lasts to -501 instead of -546. Neither page gives an area.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, years only: Egypt plus Cyprus holds -570..-546 ('In 570 BC, Cyprus was conquered by Egypt under Amasis II'; 'Egyptian rule lasted for about 25 years until 545 BC'); Cliopatria has it -550..-531

Egypt without Cyprus, holds -545..-525: Cyprus was conquered by the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great in 545; 'Cambyses II captured and later executed Psamtik III' in 525 and founded the First Egyptian Satrapy, so -524..-501 belong to the Achaemenid Empire (Twenty-seventh Dynasty)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the row, with Cyprus, to -501, 24 years after the dynasty ended (525). The Cyprus page ends Egyptian rule there in 545 ('In 545 BC, the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great conquered Cyprus'), so the shape loses Cyprus 20 years before the dynasty ends. The land is right for 524-501 but not the owner: Cliopatria's Achaemenid shape of those years holds only Sinai of Egypt, so the achaemenid-empire dossier should take over the Nile land from 525. Infobox: 'Disestablished: 525 BC'.

region.text: all of Egypt: the Delta around Sais and Upper Egypt, which Psamtik I's navy took at Thebes in 656

ledger.note: 655: Psamtik I of Sais throws off Assyrian overlordship and rules all Egypt as an independent king. 'Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE'; he 'was able to declare outright independence from Assyria'. King since 664 as an Assyrian vassal (Twenty-sixth Dynasty page: 'Established: 664 BC'; see assyrian-egypt, which holds 664-655 and dissolves into this state) and master of Thebes since 656. The year is the page's 'circa'; the region is the -615 shape.

region.text: Syria and Palestine, the 'Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt' of the page

ledger.note: 609: Necho II marches into Syria. 'In the spring of 609 BC, Necho personally led a sizable force to help the Assyrians'; he 'soon captured Kadesh on the Orontes', laid siege to Harran without taking it, and his army was 'based at Carchemish' when Nabopolassar took Kumukh. The page never says Egypt held Syria before 605, only that Nebuchadnezzar later 'conquered Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt', so the Levant is drawn as contested with Babylon (whose dossier holds it from -609) and not as an Egyptian gain; the year is the page's, the extent a reading.

region.text: Syria and Palestine, 'from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt'

ledger.note: 605: Egypt loses the Levant to Babylon at Carchemish. Nebuchadnezzar 'led them to a decisive victory over the Egyptians at Carchemish in 605 BC', 'pursued the fleeing survivors to Hamath' and 'conquered Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt'; 'Necho was unable to recover any significant part of his lost territories.' The land stays with neo-babylonian-empire.

region.text: Cyprus apart from the cells Cliopatria gives Phoenicia

ledger.note: 570: Amasis II conquers Cyprus. 'In 570 BC, Cyprus was conquered by Egypt under Amasis II.' Amasis II page: 'to this he added Cyprus' and 'the first pharaoh to conquer Cyprus after Thutmose III' (no year). No state held the island: 'the city-kingdoms of Cyprus gained independence once more' after Assyria's fall (609), so the counterpart is nobody (the Cypriot city-kingdoms, no dossier). Cliopatria dates this -550 and gives the land to its Greek City-States shape, which holds no Cyprus after 709 in the greek-city-states dossier.

region.text: the Cyprus cells of Cliopatria's Phoenicia shape of -555

ledger.note: Same year: the Phoenician cells of Cyprus (Kition's area) pass to Egypt in Cliopatria's shapes. The Cyprus page says only that 'the Phoenicians who came from Tyre colonized some cities of Cyprus, such as Idalium, Kition, Marion' and does not say Phoenicia held them in 570; kept pending the phoenicia dossier (me-04), which should carry the matching loss or let the reviewer drop this event.

545: Cyprus passes to Persia. 'Egyptian rule lasted for about 25 years until 545 BC' and 'In 545 BC, the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great conquered Cyprus'; 'the Kings of Cyprus retained their independence but had to pay tribute to their overlord' (a tributary, for the achaemenid-empire dossier). Cliopatria keeps Cyprus in this row to -501 and the Cyprus page does not mention Cambyses or 525; the page's 545 is followed.

525 BC: Cambyses II conquers Egypt. 'Cambyses II captured and later executed Psamtik III' in the First Achaemenid conquest of Egypt and founded the First Egyptian Satrapy; the Amasis II page names the 'battle of Pelusium in 525 BC'.

525 BC: the Saite Dynasty ends with the Persian conquest. Infobox 'Disestablished: 525 BC'; 'Cambyses ... founded the First Egyptian Satrapy and was crowned the first pharaoh of Dynasty XXVII'. Cliopatria keeps the row to -501.

wars.name: Saite-Babylonian conflict over the Near East and Egypt
wars.outcome: Egypt was 'driven back' from the Near East by Nebuchadnezzar II; Apries 'held back Babylonian attempts to conquer Egypt'; the Babylonian invasion of about 568-567 'gained a foothold' but 'were repelled by Amasis' forces'.
wars.note: The page names no battle, place or year before the 568-567 invasion (Amasis II page: 'In his fourth year, around 568-567 BC, Egypt was invaded by the Babylonians'), and gives no ground held either way; the Syrian phase 609-605 has its own entry with a zone and contest events (Necho II page). Psamtik II page: 'in 591 BC ... Psamtik II launched an expedition into Palestine' to foment a general Levantine revolt against the Babylonians (Kahn, cited there, dates a reconquest of the Levant 592); the outcome is not described and no ground is held, so nothing further is drawn.

wars.name: Necho II's Syrian war (Megiddo to Carchemish)

zones.text: Syria and Palestine, 'Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt'

wars.outcome: Babylonian victory: Nebuchadnezzar 'led them to a decisive victory over the Egyptians at Carchemish in 605 BC' and 'conquered Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt'; Necho 'was unable to recover any significant part of his lost territories.'
wars.note: Necho II page: Megiddo and Josiah in spring 609, Kadesh on the Orontes captured, Harran besieged and not taken, the Egyptian army at Carchemish cut off when Nabopolassar took Kumukh in 609, Carchemish 605. The page does not say Egypt held Syria in between, nor that Judah was its vassal (it says Necho deposed Jehoahaz and replaced him with Jehoiakim); neo-babylonian-empire has the 605 battle as its own war with zone Levant.

wars.name: Psamtik II's Nubian campaign
wars.outcome: Heavy Egyptian victory, no gain: 'Psamtik II led a foray into Nubia in 592 BC'; the army 'advanced to Pnubs (Kerma) and the capital city of Napata in a series of fierce battles' and inflicted 'a heavy defeat ... upon the kingdom of Kush', then 'retreated back to the First Cataract, and Elephantine continued to be the southern border of Egypt'.
wars.note: Psamtik II page: 592 BC (the Amasis II page agrees: 'a general campaign of Pharaoh Psamtik II in 592 BC in Nubia'); kingdom-of-kush dates the campaign -593 from the Napata page, a one-year difference left to that dossier. Psamtik 'does not appear to have capitalized on his victory' and the page does not say Egypt held any ground in Nubia, so no border moves and no zone is drawn.

wars.name: First Achaemenid conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Psamtik III captured and later executed; Egypt became the First Egyptian Satrapy.
wars.note: Amasis II page: 'Egypt was finally lost to the Persians during the battle of Pelusium in 525 BC'; Amasis died in 526. Only the year is given; no month, no campaign route.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the southern frontier is 'as far as the First Cataract' (a natural landmark, 'Elephantine continued to be the southern border of Egypt') and the Libyan, Sinai and Nubian edges are approximate.

sources.title: Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt
sources.note: Identity, 664 and 525, capital Sais, rulers table, 612 and 568-567 Babylonian clashes, Cambyses II in 525. Gives no area and no territorial detail (nothing on Necho II's Levant, Nubia, Cyprus, Pelusium). Its 'Established: 664 BC' is the vassal start, not independence.

sources.title: Amasis II
sources.note: Cyprus ('to this he added Cyprus', no year), the First Cataract frontier, influence in Cyrene, the 592 Nubian campaign, the 568-567 invasion, death 526, Pelusium 525.

sources.title: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
sources.note: Psamtik I installed as vassal king 664, Thebes taken 656, 'threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE'; the start of this dossier at independence. Read for the repair round.

sources.title: Ancient history of Cyprus
sources.note: Cyprus conquered by Egypt under Amasis II in 570, Egyptian rule 'until 545 BC', Achaemenid conquest under Cyrus in 545, city-kingdoms independent after Assyria. Read for the repair round.

sources.title: Necho II
sources.note: Megiddo 609, Kadesh, Harran, Carchemish 605, 'Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt' lost to Nebuchadnezzar. Read for the repair round.

sources.title: Psamtik II
sources.note: Nubian campaign 592 (Pnubs, Napata, heavy defeat of Kush, Elephantine remained the border), 591 expedition into Palestine. Read for the repair round.

notes: Repair round (2026-10-19) after the reviewer's FAIL. START MOVED to -655 (independence), the reviewer's recommended fix: assyrian-egypt (me-02, passed) holds Psamtik I's vassal kingdom 664-655 (found -664 with Lower Egypt, Upper Egypt from kingdom-of-kush in -656, dissolve -655 into this state), as do kingdom-of-kush /ledger/11 and neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/37, /40, /41, so this dossier no longer draws the Delta in 664-655: first-version keyframe -664 and the two events at -664 and -655 are replaced by one found at -655 (counterpart assyrian-egypt, the -615 shape, confidence 2, Assyrian conquest of Egypt page: 'Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE'), and the kingdom-of-kush predecessor is dropped (Upper Egypt passes Kush to assyrian-egypt in -656). The dynasty page's 'Established: 664 BC' is kept in the notes of the found event, the capital and Psamtik I's ruler entry (king from 664 as a vassal). The merge alternative (retiring assyrian-egypt) was not taken: it needs edits in three other groups' dossiers. CYPRUS rewritten from the Ancient history of Cyprus page: Egypt conquers Cyprus in 570 (Cliopatria -550, 20 years late) and loses it in 545 to Cyrus' Persia (Cliopatria keeps it to -501). The -570 gain now has counterpart nobody (the city-kingdoms: 'the city-kingdoms of Cyprus gained independence once more' after 609), because greek-city-states holds no Cyprus after 709 and neo-assyrian-empire has no Cyprus event after 709; the Phoenicia gain at -570 is kept at confidence 1 pending me-04 (the page does not say Phoenicia held Kition in 570). The -525 Cyprus loss is replaced by the -545 loss to achaemenid-empire (confidence 2) and the dissolve region is Egypt only. DISAGREEMENT left open: the Cyprus page's 545 sits 20 years before Cliopatria's end of Egyptian Cyprus and before the dynasty's end 525, and the page does not mention Cambyses; the page is followed, as the Amasis II page gives no year. The achaemenid-empire dossier (me-05) should gain Cyprus in 545 (a tributary under native kings per the page). LEVANT 609-605 (Necho II page): added as a contest_start -609 / contest_end -605 with neo-babylonian-empire over the Levant, not as a gain, because that dossier holds the Levant from -609 (its /ledger/3, gained from neo-assyrian-empire) and a second owner would draw it twice; the page says only that Nebuchadnezzar 'conquered Egyptian territory from the Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt' in 605 and does not say Egypt held Syria before (it records Kadesh captured, Harran besieged unsuccessfully, an Egyptian army at Carchemish in 609, Jehoiakim set up in Judah, never called a vassal). neo-babylonian-empire's own note ('The page does not say Egypt had held Syria before 605') and its Carchemish war are untouched; its owner may add the matching contest pair or move its Levant gain to 605. PSAMTIK II (Psamtik II page): the Nubian campaign is 592 on both Egyptian-side pages; kingdom-of-kush gives -593 (Napata page), a one-year difference left to that dossier. The result is a Kushite defeat with no Egyptian gain (the army 'retreated back to the First Cataract, and Elephantine continued to be the southern border'), so no border moves. The 591 expedition into Palestine is in the Saite-Babylonian war note, outcome not described. Unchanged from the first version: the -615..-501 Cliopatria row is reviewed as four keyframes (-655 new; -615, -550 and -530 years-only or Cyprus adjusts); Egypt after 525 holds only Sinai in Cliopatria's Achaemenid shape of -530..-501, so the achaemenid-empire dossier must add the Nile land from 525 as the First Egyptian Satrapy; no infobox area on any of the six pages, so the shapes' 452,849 and 464,287 km2 could not be compared; not on any page opened and so not in the ledger: Elephantine and Naucratis as territory, Cyrene, Tyre, Judah as a vassal, the month of Pelusium. Pages opened in all: Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt, Amasis II (first run); Assyrian conquest of Egypt, Ancient history of Cyprus, Necho II, Psamtik II (repair round, beyond the original 1-2 page budget because the reviewer named them). Gazetteer: no new names ('Levant' and 'Cyprus (island)' resolve).
